answer.rationale: Hard constraint is do not increase delivery risk with the line at 94% and no buffer and the primary contract dying in 14 days with no auto-renew. That rules out defer (c5 was non-critical month-to-month, unlike this expiry) and a primary switch (c2 cost win is real but onboarding speed vs 14 days and zero buffer is unverified and likely raises stockout TCO). Incumbent already refused to reopen price, so spending the single decision on negotiate (c4) can fail and leave no contract. Dual-source does not by itself extend the expiring primary. Renewing preserves integration and deliveries (c1) and is the only one-move option that holds supply; the 18% spend cut remains unmet and must be treated as unresolved, not solved.
